svg.title: Build the Evidence for a First Deal in 30 Days
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Build the Evidence for a First Deal in 30 Days; subtitle: Four weekly milestones prepare a controlled commercial launch.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values are milestone end days. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–4 months; this sprint establishes readiness and can finish before the first paid customer arrives.; caption: Sequence supply validation, metering, buyer qualification, and bounded activation. Do not convert an unfinished test, pending registration, or unsigned supplier offer into a completed launch claim.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one wedge and verify supplier economics; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one GPU, inference, or telecom product. Obtain written resale terms and comparable supplier quotes, classify applicable service duties, and model utilization break-even without treating prepaid deposits as revenue.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build the wallet, meter, and controlled shutdown path; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Connect a Stripe test flow to an internal credit ledger. Replay duplicate events, supplier outages, and exhausted balances; test tenant isolation and retention settings before enabling customer production credentials.; label: Days 15-21; value: Qualify buyers and prove a bounded service benchmark; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Conduct discovery with named buyers and benchmark authorized workloads or traffic. Complete applicable carrier provisioning and registrations, document service limits, and reject pilots whose effective unit economics fail the price floor.; label: Days 22-30; value: Run an eligible pilot or finish readiness evidence; numeric value: 30.0; detail: If contracts, funding, and applicable service requirements are complete, activate a capped pilot and reconcile daily. Otherwise finish test evidence and buyer follow-up without buying speculative capacity or claiming a completed deal.

text.title: Build the Evidence for a First Deal in 30 Days
text.tspan: Build the Evidence for a First Deal in 30 Days

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one wedge and verify supplier economics; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one GPU, inference, or telecom product. Obtain written resale terms and comparable supplier quotes, classify applicable service duties, and model utilization break-even without treating prepaid deposits as revenue.

text.title: Select one wedge and verify supplier economics

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Build the wallet, meter, and controlled shutdown path; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Connect a Stripe test flow to an internal credit ledger. Replay duplicate events, supplier outages, and exhausted balances; test tenant isolation and retention settings before enabling customer production credentials.

text.title: Build the wallet, meter, and controlled shutdown path

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Qualify buyers and prove a bounded service benchmark; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Conduct discovery with named buyers and benchmark authorized workloads or traffic. Complete applicable carrier provisioning and registrations, document service limits, and reject pilots whose effective unit economics fail the price floor.

text.title: Qualify buyers and prove a bounded service benchmark

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Run an eligible pilot or finish readiness evidence; numeric value: 30.0; detail: If contracts, funding, and applicable service requirements are complete, activate a capped pilot and reconcile daily. Otherwise finish test evidence and buyer follow-up without buying speculative capacity or claiming a completed deal.

text.title: Run an eligible pilot or finish readiness evidence
Assumptions: Numeric values are milestone end days. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–4 months; this sprint establishes readiness and can finish before the first paid customer arrives.
